Hi Emma — great to meet you on the call earlier. Attaching the draft Order Form that references our standard MSA. Two quick things you said you wanted explicitly clarified for legal/procurement: 1) whether NexGen retains ownership of model outputs, and 2) whether your data/output can be used to train Redwood models or otherwise improve the service.

Summary of our starting positions (in the draft):
- Output ownership: customer retains rights to customer outputs (standard carveout for productization).
- Feedback license: Redwood asks for a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use customer feedback (prompts, anonymized telemetry) to improve models and the service.
- Training: by default our platform may use deidentified logs/telemetry to improve models; we can discuss a per-customer opt-out.

I'm attaching the Order Form and a marked-up redline that flags the IP clauses. Can you confirm the list of must-haves from NexGen so we can move this to legal redlines? We can propose narrowed language if helpful.

Thanks Marissa — quick points from our side after internal review:
- NexGen must have exclusive ownership of outputs we generate for product features that are customer-facing. We need to be able to commercialize derived assets.
- We need an explicit opt-out for any use of our raw customer data or outputs for model training (including fine-tuning). PII must never be used.
- If Redwood requires a feedback license to improve the service, we need it scoped to: (a) aggregated, non-personal telemetry; (b) time-limited (e.g., 18 months); and (c) explicitly exclude any content that could re-identify our customers.

Thanks for the flag. High-level legal position and suggested compromise language below; see inline snippet that we can place into the Order Form / MSA as an exhibit. We should also provide a short summary packet for NexGen's counsel showing how opt-out works operationally and what telemetry we need for reliability.

Legal guidance (proposed compromise):
- Output Ownership: "Customer shall retain ownership of Customer Outputs. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer Outputs to provide the Services to Customer and to perform debugging and billing." This preserves productization carveouts customers often request — but if NexGen requires exclusive title with no license back for service provision, we will need a narrowly scoped license back to operate the service (see bracketed alternative).

- Training & Feedback License: Insert a two-track approach:
  1) Training Opt-Out: "Upon Customer's written election in the Order Form, Redwood will not use Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve any model weights. Redwood may still process Customer Content for provisioning, maintenance, and debug purposes as necessary to provide the Services."
  2) Scoped Feedback License: "Customer grants Redwood a limited, revocable license to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and service performance metrics (which do not include Customer Content or Outputs and cannot be used to re-identify individuals) to improve the Services. Such telemetry will be retained for a maximum period of 18 months unless otherwise agreed in writing."

- PII / Re-identification carveouts: Add explicit prohibition on use of identified PII for training and require Redwood to adopt industry-standard de-identification measures. Also offer to add audit/evidence commitments (e.g., SOC 2 summary + third-party attestation) to reassure counsel.

Please confirm whether the "license back for service provision" wording is acceptable to sales (we can try the bracketed alternative if NexGen insists on a clean transfer of output title). Karhik/priyom — can you confirm technical feasibility and any edge cases? I will prepare redline text for the MSA exhibit if you approve.

Short technical note and implementation plan:
- Feasibility: We can implement a per-customer "training opt-out" flag at the account level. When active, the data pipeline will drop any Customer Content / Outputs from any training or fine-tuning ingestion flows. This is straightforward for our central training pipeline (we already tag dataset provenance).
- Telemetry: We cannot completely eliminate ephemeral runtime logs because they are used for real-time debugging and safety (e.g., prompt traces to diagnose failures). However, we can implement: (a) automatic PII scrubbing for runtime logs, and (b) a separate telemetry export that only contains aggregated metrics and hashed, non-reversible identifiers for internal analytics.
- Retention: We can set telemetry retention to 18 months configurable per-customer. Longer retention would be possible but should be opt-in.
- Edge cases: Debugging a data-specific model failure may require transient access to de-identified traces; we propose documented process for such escalations and notifications to the customer.

Timeline to ship flags + policy: 2 sprints (about 4 weeks) for the opt-out switch, scrubbing pipeline, and retention config. We can scope initial go-live to exclude training ingestion; follow-on audit tooling would take an additional sprint.

I'll prepare a short note (1 page) describing operational controls we can share with NexGen counsel.

— Karhik

Hi Emma — thank you for the clear guidance. Per our internal review (legal + product), here is a proposed compromise we can implement and include in the Order Form:

1) Outputs: NexGen retains ownership of Customer Outputs. Redwood will include narrow license language necessary to operate the service (provisioning, debugging, billing). If NexGen prefers absolute title with no license back, please flag and we'll escalate.

2) Training opt-out: We will add a written election in the Order Form that prevents Redwood from using Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train or fine-tune Redwood models.

3) Scoped feedback license: Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified telemetry and service performance metrics (explicitly excluding Customer Content and outputs) to improve the Services. Retention limited to 18 months.

4) PII & de-identification: We will never use identified PII for training. We will apply industry-standard de-identification and can provide SOC 2 summary and a one-page operational controls note explaining how the opt-out works.

Next steps:
- I've attached an updated redline (NexGen_redlines_v1.docx) with the language above.
